text:
Evan: hey team — first day! quick blocker: i'm tethering to my phone hotspot and on the split-tunnel WireGuard i can't reach the bastion (rdw-bastion.company.internal) or the internal artifact server at 10.60.8.5. office wifi works. macOS Sonoma on an M1. any quick wins?

Maya (Infra): welcome Evan :) Mobile ISP often uses CG-NAT and sometimes prefers IPv6 which can break hairpinning. Can you paste `route get 10.60.8.5` and `ifconfig` and `scutil --dns`? Also does `dig internal-artifact.company.internal @10.200.4.2` return a v4 address?

Evan: pasted below — sorry it's a lot
```
$ route get 10.60.8.5
10.60.8.5 via 100.64.1.1 dev en0 src 192.168.43.210
    cache
$ ifconfig utun3
utun3: flags=8051<UP,POINTOPOINT,RUNNING,MULTICAST> mtu 1380
  inet 10.200.1.9 --> 10.200.1.9 netmask 0xffffffff
$ scutil --dns
resolver #1
  nameserver[0] : 10.200.4.2

$ dig internal-artifact.company.internal @10.200.4.2 +short
10.60.8.5
```
so DNS resolves to 10.60.8.5 but connecting times out. traceroute just shows my phone AP then nothing.

Ravi (SRE): yep that's classic mobile CG-NAT. two low-friction options: 1) force-route the internal prefix over utun3 so packets don't egress to the phone NAT: `sudo route -n add -net 10.60.0.0/16 -interface utun3` (replace utun3 with yours). 2) use our public bounce host with per-user forward (rdw-bounce-us.company.com) — it's designed for users who can't hairpin. Example `ssh -J evan@rdw-bounce-us rdw-bastion` or add ProxyJump to your ssh config.

Evan: tried the `route` command and pings now reach 10.60.8.5, build downloads ok. is the route persistent across reboots?

Maya (Infra): macOS route commands aren't persistent. if you want persistent on mac you can add a small launchd script to run at login or use `networksetup -setv6off <service>` for the tether interface sometimes helps but fiddly. for onboarding we usually recommend using the bounce host or the SSH SOCKS for short-lived work.

Evan: what's the SOCKS flow? i use Docker a lot for the onboarding script which pulls images from internal registry.

Ravi (SRE): socks is handy — `ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_rdw -D 1080 evan@rdw-bastion` then set `HTTP_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` and `HTTPS_PROXY=socks5://localhost:1080` before `docker pull` or `docker build`. Docker Desktop honors those env vars. Alternatively use `ssh -J evan@rdw-bounce-us -- docker build -t me/img - < Dockerfile` to run the build inside the bounce host (we have a small runner).

Maya (Infra): added note: mobile hotspots can also provide IPv6-only address families which confuses some clients. if `curl -4 -v http://10.60.8.5` works but `curl` without `-4` doesn't, you have an IPv6 preference issue. `sudo sysctl -w net.inet6.ip6.v6only=0` is mac-specific and risky — prefer bounce/route.

Evan: socks approach worked for my Docker pulls quickly. i'll stick with that during onboarding. thanks! :tada:

Onboard Bot: Created INF-756: "Onboarding: mobile hotspot / CG-NAT note + bounce host doc" assigned to Infrastructure.

Maya (Infra): i'll add a short FAQ entry: "If you tether to a phone and internal services time out, try SOCKS via bastion or ssh ProxyJump to rdw-bounce-us. Persistent macOS routes are optional; we don't recommend modifying system IPv6 settings unless you know the impact."

Evan: leaving this here for other mobile-first folks — appreciate the help!
